description: Explore product intent as a sparring partner, resolve consequential choices, and shape narrow composable features with independent acceptance before authorized delivery.

# Shape

Work with the user to understand the problem and choose a useful outcome. A polished request or a feasible implementation is not necessarily a complete brief. Use this in greenfield and brownfield work; depth follows uncertainty and consequence, not project age.

## Start The Goal

- Reuse or create the scoped native Goal under the standing user request. Do not ask again.
- Build scope ends at final review; specification-only scope grants no build authority.
- Set budgets only when supplied. Honor overrides, interruptions, and tool/runtime limits.
- Never replace an unrelated Goal, extend limits, or create substitute persistence loops.
- If Goal tools are unavailable, report once and continue authorized work. Preserve other ownership; stopped is not complete.

## Discover And Decide

Default to co-discovery, not immediate specification. Inspect the request, relevant dialogue, repository behavior, existing decisions, and supplied references. Explain the current understanding and a recommended direction before turning a broad brief into contracts. Keep exploration conversational until a decision is worth recording.

Connect the problem, user experience, and technical context: who encounters what situation, why the present behavior is inadequate, what useful result changes, and how architecture or provider constraints affect that result. Investigate the surrounding journey and affected consumers without requiring an exhaustive repository tour. Code establishes what happens, not necessarily what should happen.

Challenge a proposed solution when a materially different interpretation or simpler approach would better meet the need. Give the reason, practical consequence, and recommendation. Do not manufacture objections or treat every choice as unresolved.

- Resolve discoverable facts and routine engineering yourself. Ask for user context you cannot inspect and choices that change experience, scope, ownership, compatibility, cost, permissions, or meaningful risk.
- Use concrete examples and focused groups of questions. Questions can uncover the problem, test assumptions, or explore alternatives; they are not limited to blockers or multiple-choice decisions already identified.
- After answers or corrections, explain what changed and what remains open. Continue useful rounds when new consequential uncertainty appears. An answer settles its own decision; announcing an interpretation is not agreement.
- Distinguish accepted decisions, recommendations, and assumptions. Infer reversible low-risk details when appropriate; do not freeze a consequential unsupported interpretation as accepted behavior.
- Continue independent investigation and settled work while questions are pending. No question quota, compulsory questionnaire, or new sign-off. A clear request can proceed directly.

Select investigation lenses from the actual journey. For defaults or automation, inspect first use, absent configuration, eligibility, overrides, retries, and unavailable providers as relevant. For a usable application, trace entry/startup, real integrations, user actions, and visible saved results. Component success may leave that journey incomplete. Use a small visual comparison or authorized experiment when it will resolve uncertainty better than more prose; planning alone grants no implementation or new access.

## Shape Narrow Slices

Prefer one specific, independently demonstrable outcome per feature. Include the minimal end-to-end path and necessary failure/permission behavior. Split when outcomes can be accepted separately, decisions remain independent, or one uncertain integration would hold unrelated value hostage. Do not split merely by files or layers, or omit essential cases to make a spec look small.

For a broad request, maintain a short journey outline showing how slices connect, their dependencies, and deferred choices. Prepare the next useful slice in detail; keep later slices provisional until their decisions are ready. Do not require a complete backlog of executable proofs before delivering a settled slice. Continue toward every authorized outcome rather than quietly dropping later scope.

I recommend starting with **members seeing their own upcoming bookings**, then adding booking actions as separate, narrow features. The order should reflect what creates the most work at reception.

The repository is a small starting point. [README.md](/private/tmp/flexible-discovery-candidate-studio/README.md:2) describes a staff booking desk, but [studio.py](/private/tmp/flexible-discovery-candidate-studio/studio.py:4) only reads and prints a sample schedule. I ran it successfully. There is no implemented booking workflow, member sign-in, or saving of changes. [schedule.json](/private/tmp/flexible-discovery-candidate-studio/schedule.json:1) contains one class, one booking, and a member credit balance.

My proposed first feature is **“See my upcoming bookings.”** A member securely identifies themselves, sees their scheduled classes, and gets a clear empty state when they have none. They can only access their own bookings. Acceptance would demonstrate this with two different members against the same authoritative records reception uses. This gives us a useful first result while establishing member access and shared data.

The rest can stay provisional:

| Feature | Demonstrable outcome |
|---|---|
| See remaining credits | A member sees an accurate balance with a clear meaning. |
| Book a class | A member reserves an eligible place and sees the saved booking. |
| Cancel a booking | A member releases their place and sees the credit consequence. |
| Move a booking | A member changes sessions; an unsuccessful move preserves their original booking. |
| Join a waiting list | A member joins or leaves a full class’s queue and can see their status. |

Each feature needs its own complete journey. For example, booking must handle two people attempting the last place; moving must avoid losing the original session before securing the replacement. Reception and members should operate on one shared record.

Before turning the first feature into a specification, I’d like to settle three things:

1. **Where is the biggest operational pain?** New bookings, moving sessions, full classes, or credit questions? Are these all group classes, or do “sessions” include private appointments?
2. **Where do your real records live today?** Is this repository a prototype, or does reception use it? What currently records bookings, member identities, and pass purchases?
3. **What does a remaining credit mean?** The sample gives Avery five credits and an existing booking. Are those five already net of that booking, and do you deduct credits when booking or attending?

Cancellation cutoffs and waiting-list promotion can be settled when shaping those features. They need business decisions, but needn’t delay an agreed read-only first release.

No files changed.

The first feature is now scoped to viewing upcoming bookings from a staff-imported CSV, with email-code sign-in and a visible refresh time. I’ll write the specification and leave application changes and acceptance proof out of this task.

## Schema

Adopted repositories require version-2 `docs/features/status.json`; the gate uses `--require-feature-status` (automatic for this harness). A feature entry has exactly `id`, `feature_dir`, `priority`, `status`, `owner`, `proof_run`, `notes`, inside `{"version": 2, "features": [...]}`. IDs/directories/priorities are unique; paths are safe repository-relative. Use a stable task id (unique task token if unavailable) as owner, nonempty only while active. Notes are concise lifecycle context, not a task list or evidence store.

Every persisted entry owns a nonempty FEATURE. Draft and blocked entries may lack proof while decisions or prerequisites remain open; ready/active packages require nonempty PROOF and executable `proof/run.sh`. These checks establish structure, not semantic readiness or independent authorship. `done` points to the latest official run physically under its own `proof/runs/`, with `result.json` PASS; foreign, symlinked, missing, malformed, failed, or newer-incomplete evidence cannot qualify. Explicit regression-kind results never qualify; historical proof-only results may omit kind. Other states have null proof pointers; retain prior files.

Every new transition to done also requires an unchanged captured candidate and a matching independent PASS review receipt binding the proof and selected supporting runs. See [capture and receipt commands](evidence.md#current-candidate-and-review). Reading existing done entries accepts historical evidence formats without comparing all old source states with today's checkout. Reopening one requires fresh evidence under the current completion contract; old acceptance does not replace current regression assurance.

## Mutation And Ownership

```bash
"${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/scripts/feature_status.py" --root REPO --id FEATURE --owner TASK --from new --to draft
"${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/scripts/feature_status.py" --root REPO --id FEATURE --owner TASK --from ready --to active
"${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/scripts/feature_status.py" --root REPO --id FEATURE --owner TASK --from active --to done --proof-run docs/features/FEATURE/proof/runs/RUN
```

Normal states: draft (decisions/proof incomplete), ready (decision-complete runnable independent proof), active (owned work), blocked (necessary unresolved dependency), done (owning skill's proof/review completion satisfied). Reopen done->active for a contract defect or done->draft for accepted behavior changes, retaining history. Active work can return to draft/blocked or ready on explicit preemption; only the user can authorize acceptance changes. Independent setup repair stays active.

Select explicit/current-task work first, then the task's resumable claim; global lowest ready priority applies only to requested queue continuation. Coordinate overlapping files/runtime writes; stabilize only relevant verification inputs. Optional worktrees require reconciliation on integration. No automatic takeover/lease exists: user-authorized handoff confirms the prior task stopped, releases its claim active->ready with its recorded owner, then the receiver claims it. Owner tokens coordinate; they are not authentication.

Feature state and Goal state are distinct. Interruption/exhaustion is unfinished, never done or automatically a native blocked state. Apply native tool criteria independently. A completion pointer write after final review needs the gate, not new proof solely for metadata.

If absent, initialize the empty v2 index. If older/unversioned, archive its exact original under `docs/harness/migrations/`, then use a one-off conversion under the helper's same sidecar lock: reread, validate identities/priorities/ownership, and atomically replace. Never replace existing data with an empty index. Preserve identities, relative priorities, owners, contracts, and evidence. Preserve done with structurally valid retained historical proof; otherwise blocked with a reason and null pointer. Mark missing historical context incomplete without fabricating proof; do not rebuild/re-prove history. Corruption or conflicting ownership needs resolution, not invented values.

Migration is authorized local setup, not another approval/Goal question. After conversion, return to the helper for registration/transitions; do not add compatibility readers.

+# View my upcoming bookings
+
+Status: draft specification. Application implementation and acceptance-proof authoring are explicitly outside this task. This document records the agreed first feature and identifies the remaining delivery prerequisites; it does not declare implementation readiness.
+
+## Outcome and context
+
+Members can answer “Which upcoming classes am I booked into?” without messaging reception. They verify their email, see only their own upcoming bookings, and can judge how current the information is from a visible refresh time.
+
+The repository is a prototype: `studio.py` reads and prints `schedule.json`. Reception's spreadsheet is the authoritative booking record. All sessions are group classes. This feature publishes a read-only copy of that record; it does not change bookings or replace reception's booking process.
+
+## Confirmed scope
+
+- Reception manually imports a CSV containing `member_email`, `member_name`, `class_id`, and `starts_at`.
+- Each member has one unique email. Members sign in with a code sent to that email and only see their own bookings.
+- The member view shows when the booking data was last refreshed.
+- Payments stay at reception. Credit display, new bookings, moves, cancellations, and waiting lists are deferred. Credits are already net of existing bookings, but this feature does not consume or expose them.
+
+## Member journey and visible behavior
+
+1. A member opens the member booking page and enters their email. The page explains that a sign-in code will be sent by email and offers code entry and resend.
+2. A valid, unused code establishes an authenticated session for that verified email. Invalid, expired, or already-used codes cannot grant access. A member can sign out; expired sessions require sign-in again.
+3. The page reads the latest successfully imported data and displays that member's classes with future start times, ordered soonest first. Each entry shows `class_id` and its date and time, with an explicit time-zone label. The CSV contains no class title, venue, duration, or instructor, so this feature does not invent those details or require extra columns.
+4. “Last refreshed” shows the time the latest import completed successfully. Adjacent text explains that the page reflects reception's latest import and directs members to reception if something looks wrong. This timestamp is not represented as the spreadsheet's last edit time.
+5. A verified email with no matching upcoming bookings sees a clear empty state and the refresh time. A class ceases to be upcoming when its start time is reached; attendance and completed-class history are outside scope.
+
+Before any successful import, show that booking information has not yet been published, without a fabricated refresh time or prototype sample bookings. A data-service failure shows an unavailable state with a retry route, rather than a misleading empty list.
+
+## Manual refresh and data boundaries
+
+Recommended import contract, pending confirmation with reception: every CSV is a complete snapshot of the bookings to publish. A successful import replaces the previous published snapshot, so bookings removed or corrected in the spreadsheet are reflected after refresh. Do not infer deletions from a partial export. The import mechanism must make the replacement behavior clear to its operator.
+
+Use a staff-only operator import command for the first release, consistent with the current terminal workflow. A staff management interface, scheduled spreadsheet sync, and public upload endpoint are unnecessary for this outcome. Staff require access to the deployed data store; members receive no import permission.
+
+Validate the entire file before publication: required headers and values, usable email addresses, and parseable, unambiguous start times. Reject invalid input with useful row-level errors. Treat a booking as the combination of member email, class ID, and start time; repeated identical rows do not create duplicate displayed bookings. Apply the same email normalization to import and sign-in, trimming surrounding whitespace and comparing consistently without rewriting aliases.
+
+Publish the validated snapshot and its refresh timestamp together. Members must never see a partially imported file. An unsuccessful import preserves both the previous snapshot and its refresh time; the operator receives an explicit failure. A header-only file must not silently erase all published bookings: require an explicit operator confirmation of the empty replacement. Reimporting a valid snapshot is safe and updates its refresh time.
+
+## Access and dependencies
+
+Filter bookings on the server using the authenticated, verified email, including on reload and direct data requests. A requested email, member name, or class ID supplied by the browser cannot broaden access. Do not expose the raw CSV, member directory, other members' bookings, or sign-in codes to members. Keep imported files outside public web assets and avoid logging codes or full imported records.
+
+Email-code delivery must use a real email service in the eventual deployed environment. Codes must expire, be single-use, and have bounded verification and resend attempts. Sign-in responses must not reveal whether another address appears in the booking data. Failure to request or deliver a code needs a recoverable message; no authentication fallback may skip email verification.

The existing print-only program and sample JSON establish none of those capabilities. Keep payments and reception's spreadsheet workflow compatible; no write-back to the spreadsheet is included.

+- Confirm the studio's time zone and the actual `starts_at` format. Prefer timestamps with explicit UTC offsets. Member-visible times use the agreed studio zone.
+- Establish the intended hosting environment, staff access to its import path, and an authorized email sender/service. Email provider capability and delivery have not been verified in this task. Provider choice, credentials, and deployment are not authorized by this specification alone.
+- Author the independent acceptance proof in a subsequent task when requested. There are no proof scripts, fixtures, run results, or readiness claims in this package.
+
+Only this first feature is specified. Later credit and booking-action features remain provisional and need their own business rules and acceptance boundaries.
